title: Flaky required check: concurrent creates in separate processes serialize
description:
Filed from WCLI-9 on opum-agent's kickoff. The required check on dev is not deterministic: the case "T06: transactions > concurrent creates in separate processes serialize: one wins, one refuses" failed the first Check run of opum-ai/ward-cli#60 and then dev's own push run at 8446ffc, passing on re-run both times, while an identical source tree passed at 7cbd9cc. Two failures in four runs of one tree. It holds a merge until someone re-runs it, so it costs every session that lands work, and a red required context that means nothing is a signal everyone learns to ignore.

Not a WCLI-9 defect: the tree that failed is byte-identical to the tree that passed. The case belongs to WCLI-6's area (encrypted SQLite store, transactional mutation), but it lives in the test suite rather than in that closed task.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The failure is measured and recorded: the exact commits, the runs that failed and passed, the runner, and the failing output captured verbatim at least once -- or the recorded runs show it did not reproduce, with the same detail

The case is deterministic on the required Check context: the change that made it so is named in the notes (the fix, or a quarantine naming the reason and what unblocks it), and no run after it is recorded as failing on this case alone

plan: 2. Apply the preserved fix: settledLayout/requireSettledVault for the pre-lock reads in create and mutate; leave read alone as verified-safe
3. Re-verify the mechanism with the instrumented reproducer (pre-fix hits, post-fix zero) rather than trusting the scratch copies
4. bun run check green; store tests 40/40
5. Independent review per spec 15; PR into dev; required Check green on the head SHA
6. Record AC1/AC2 evidence on the task, close it in the PR, squash merge, prune the local branch
7. Promote dev to main so the tracker-only commits ride it
implementationNotes: THE CHANGE THAT MADE IT DETERMINISTIC (AC2). settledLayout(db) = db.transaction(() => layoutOf(db)).deferred() in src/adapters/sqlite-vault-store.ts; create's pre-lock layoutOf check and mutate's pre-lock requireVault (now requireSettledVault) use it, so the three layout reads are taken in one snapshot and a concurrent create's commit cannot land between them. The in-transaction checks keep plain layoutOf — inside a write transaction the lock already settles the layout. read and header were verified already-safe and are recorded as verified, NOT fixed: read's requireVault already sits inside db.transaction(() => ...).deferred() and header's layoutOf likewise; neither was changed. Survey for other unwrapped multi-statement pre-lock reads: none — inspect()'s headerVersions is a single 20-byte readSync, a different shape with no multi-statement window. New test "a commit can land between bare reads and cannot land inside a read transaction" pins the premise: bare reads interleave a commit, a read transaction cannot (the committing writer is refused while the snapshot is held). Local evidence on the branch tree: bun run check green (typecheck, lint, format, layer check 46 files 0 violations, 624/624 tests); test/vault-store.test.ts 40/40; and the file run 20 more consecutive times, 0 failures.

MEASUREMENT (AC1), re-verified this session against the API, the raw logs and the objects rather than taken from WCLI-42. Two required Check failures on one source tree: run 36520676744 attempt 1 — PR opum-ai/ward-cli#60's first Check, event pull_request, 2026-09-29T04:13:36Z, head 9b0f7f72e768b6c3835e64901d1ab2340c988860 — Check failed on runner linux-arm64-dccd7-runner-dpj5l while Tracker integrity and Docs passed in the same attempt; and run 36521526949 attempt 1 — dev's push at 8446ffc647ccd5c658a0b5ddfe1999d7c498876d, event push, 04:25:00Z — Check failed on runner linux-arm64-dccd7-runner-s7g2n. Both attempt 2 passed. The passing comparison run: push run 36519874011 attempt 1 at 7cbd9ccfb0d8b8c9149a648fdf829339a8742857 (04:03:15Z) passed all three jobs — and verified by diff, not by the tree hash (a tracker-only commit moves that): 7cbd9cc's src/test tree is byte-identical to the failing pair's, because 7cbd9cc -> 8446ffc touches .quest/tasks/WCLI-9.json alone, one line. So the same source tree both failed and passed. Verbatim from run 36520676744 attempt 1: "448 | expect([...outcomes].sort()).toEqual(["created", "vault_exists"]);" with "error: expect(received).toEqual(expected)" — received ["created", "vault_store_unrecognized"] against expected ["created", "vault_exists"], then "(fail) T06: transactions > concurrent creates in separate processes serialize: one wins, one refuses". Mechanism re-measured this session with the instrumented pre-fix reproducer (/tmp/ward-repro): create-vs-create 3 mismatches in 3000 iterations, each carrying "WARD-DEBUG layoutOf id=0 version=0|1 schema=1"; mutate-vs-create 0/2500 then 0/4000 (WCLI-42 measured 3/2500 in its own run; this session's two are recorded no-hits at the same harness); read-vs-create 0/1500. Post-fix against the branch tree (/tmp/ward-postfix): create 0/3000, mutate 0/2500, read 0/1500.

VALIDATING RUNS (the runs after the change, AC2's second half), each read from the API rather than inferred. Every required context reported green on every head the branch carried: on the fix commit 3d092478 — PR opum-ai/ward-cli#82's Check, run 36542100507, completed 2026-09-29T08:21:06Z, Docs and Tracker integrity green on the same SHA; on the pin commit 9bedc4d — Check run 36543820890; on the region-pin commit 45941a9 — Check run 36544480559; on the head bb6bbcd — Check run 36545140201, completed 08:49:52Z, with the PR reading mergeStateStatus CLEAN. No run after the change is recorded failing on this case. Local corroboration: test/vault-store.test.ts 41/41 plus 20 further consecutive runs of the file at 0 failures, against a pre-fix tree on which the required Check failed both first attempts of the two runs that hit it, and an independent flake hunt that measured 4 failures in 360 pre-fix T06 runs (1/60 then 4/300) against 0/360 post-fix.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW (spec 15), this session, an opum-workflow reviewer, three rounds against three successive heads. ROUND 1 (the fix, 3d09247): verdict — correct, no defect found. It confirmed the mechanism deterministically rather than statistically: a commit made to land between layoutOf's header reads and its schema read yields exactly the mixed state (application_id=0, user_version=0, schema=["vault"]) refused as vault_store_unrecognized; inside one deferred transaction both header reads and the schema read come from one snapshot, the read lock is taken by layoutOf's first statement, and the writer's COMMIT is refused immediately until the snapshot ends. Error-path and lock-timing parity were probed on scratch stores; no other unwrapped multi-statement pre-lock read exists — headerVersions is a single 20-byte readSync. Its independent flake hunt on a pristine origin/dev archive: 4 failures in 360 T06 runs (1/60 then 4/300), all received vault_store_unrecognized against expected vault_exists, against 0/360 on the fixed tree. Findings: F1 — a revert of the two call sites kept the suite green; closed by the source-level pin. F2 — the premise test's refused assertion accepts any Error rather than specifically the lock refusal; ACCEPTED, because an unrelated error on the commit attempt still means the commit did not land, which is the property the test asserts. F3 — T06 remains busy-timeout-failable by design; ACCEPTED, because that is ADR 0001's documented contract ("past the busy timeout they report vault_busy") and the test pins the outcome pair, not the lock timing. ROUND 2 (the pin, 9bedc4d): falsified — a swap of the settled and bare spellings between the pre-lock and in-transaction checks kept the presence-only pin green while the flake returned (1 failure in 600 T06 runs on the swapped tree), and a comment carrying the settled text over a reverted call site did the same. ROUND 3 (the region pin, 45941a9): held against every revert, swap and insertion shape tried, but four deliberately-placed shapes stayed green — a bare read after the heal, a bare read inside a helper the region cannot see (for create and for mutate), and a spoofing comment with the bare read relocated. All four were closed in bb6bbcd by counting the file's bare reads (exactly four layoutOf, exactly two requireVault) in addition to the region checks, with each region now ending at the immediate transaction. The pin's stated boundary, written into its own comment and not hidden: it sees src/adapters/sqlite-vault-store.ts only — a bare read moved to another module, or reached through an alias, is outside what it can prove. ROUND 4 (the hardened pin, bb6bbcd): explicit verdict — clean for what was asked: R1-R4 red, clean 41/41, the whole gate 625/625, and no same-spelling bare pre-lock read survives either the regions or the counts. Named and accepted as outside the pin's proof: a same-file helper spelling the bare read with a different argument name, and an alias — both deliberately-placed paraphrases, where a literal revert is caught by the counts. One inaccurate sentence in the pin's own count comment (it claimed an aliased spelling moves the counts; it does not) was corrected in the same branch, and the boundary comment now names the different-argument-name case too.
finalSummary: Fixed the flaky required check on dev. create's pre-lock layoutOf and mutate's pre-lock requireVault read the SQLite layout in three statements outside any transaction, so a concurrent create's commit could land between them and hand back a state that never existed — its vault table present, its header fields not yet — which layoutOf refused as vault_store_unrecognized instead of answering vault_exists. settledLayout() now takes those three reads in one deferred transaction, used by create and by mutate through requireSettledVault; the in-transaction checks keep plain layoutOf, and read and header were verified already-safe inside their own deferred transactions and are recorded as verified, not fixed. A premise test pins that bare reads interleave a commit and a read transaction cannot, and a source-level pin holds create's and mutate's pre-lock regions to the settled form with the file's bare reads counted, so a revert, a swap, a hidden bare read or a spoofing comment reddens the suite instead of resurfacing as a statistical flake; its boundary — it sees that one file — is stated in the test. Verified from primary sources: the two failing CI runs re-read from the API and raw logs (runs 36520676744 attempt 1 and 36521526949 attempt 1, each failing only the Check job, verbatim received ["created", "vault_store_unrecognized"] against expected ["created", "vault_exists"] at test/vault-store.test.ts:448), with the passing comparison run at 7cbd9cc shown by diff to carry a byte-identical src/test tree (a one-line tracker record being the only difference); the instrumented pre-fix reproducer reproduced 3 mismatches in 3000 with the WARD-DEBUG mixed-read signature; the same harness post-fix 0/3000, mutate 0/2500, read 0/1500; an independent flake hunt measured 4/360 pre-fix against 0/360 post-fix; bun run check green (625/625); and the required Check green on every head the branch carried (runs 36542100507, 36543820890, 36544480559, 36545140201). Independent review per spec 15 found the fix correct with no defect; its findings against the pin were each closed by a committed control, and its two accepted limitations (any-Error assertion; busy-timeout-failable T06) are recorded on the task.
